conduct.chirper.appropriate.4: Graphic sexual language intended for arousal

conduct.velvet.adults.body: Velvet is for adults aged 18 and above. Any content involving minors, child-like characters (including Lalafell and Kitten Mods), or underage roleplay is strictly prohibited and results in a permanent ban.

conduct.velvet.limits.lead: Velvet is an adult space, but some content is still off-limits:
conduct.velvet.limits.1: Animal genitalia, including animal genitals on humanoid or beast-race characters

settings.title: Settings
settings.vibrationHint: The phone shakes briefly when a notification arrives.
settings.quietWhileBusyHint: Hold banners, sound and vibration during combat, duties, cutscenes and loading. Notifications still arrive.
settings.showNotificationBannerHint: Display banner notifications at the top of the screen.
settings.lockPositionHint: The phone stays where you put it, and dragging inside it scrolls instead of moving the window.
settings.marketContextMenuHint: Shows "Search the Market" option in the in-game context menu when right-clicking on an item.
settings.scrollWhileIdleHint: Your character scrolls through their phone (Tomescroll emote) while standing still and out of combat. Does nothing if you haven't unlocked the emote.
settings.showInGposeHint: Keep the phone available while you're in Group Pose, so you can open it during photo shoots. Turn it off to keep your screen clear for screenshots.
settings.nativeFileDialogHint: Pick photos and sounds with the Windows file browser. Turn it off if importing a file crashes your game.
settings.chirperShowPhotosHint: Chirps that carry photos show up in your feeds on Chirper. Turn this off to hide photo chirps from your feeds.
settings.chirperShowGifsHint: Chirps that carry animated GIFs show up in your feeds on Chirper. Turn this off to hide GIF chirps from your feeds.
settings.chirperShowReplyMediaHint: Photos and GIFs attached to replies show under the reply text on Chirper. Turn this off to keep replies text only.
settings.aethergramShowGifsHint: Grams that carry an animated GIF show up in your feeds on Aethergram. Turn this off to keep your feeds photos only.
settings.aethergramShowCommentMediaHint: Photos and GIFs attached to comments show under the comment text on Aethergram. Turn this off to keep comments text only.
settings.showSensitiveHint: Photos marked sensitive stay covered until you tap them. Turn this on to see them straight away.
settings.startupHint: Open the phone automatically when you log in. Open minimized shows it as a small dock that you tap to expand.
onboarding.searchTourBody: Pull down on the Home Screen or tap Search to find apps, contacts, settings, notes, and market items in one place.
settings.gameSoundsHint: Sound effects in the arcade mini-games.
settings.silentModeHint: Mutes the ringtone, notifications, and interface sounds in one tap. Media keeps playing.
settings.ringtoneHint: Play a ringtone when a call comes in.
settings.notificationSoundsHint: Play a sound when a notification arrives.
settings.uiSoundsHint: Short sounds for key moments: waking the phone, taking a photo, sending a message, earning coins.
settings.uiSoundExtrasHint: Extra feedback for frequent interactions. Turn off any that feel noisy.
settings.soundImportHint: Imported files appear in the list below and play at the volume set here, separate from the game's own sound settings.
settings.supportHint: Aetherphone is free and made in my spare time. If you enjoy it, a pledge on Patreon helps me keep building and improving it. Thank you for being here.
settings.tutorialsHint: Tips appear once the first time you open each app. Reset to see them all again.
settings.tellArchive: Save tell history on this PC
settings.tellArchiveHint: Tells are saved as plain text files on this PC so conversations survive a restart. They are never uploaded anywhere. Turn this off to keep new tells in memory only. Deleting a conversation also deletes its file.
settings.chatPrivacyHint: These apply to the Message app. If you turn read receipts or last seen off, you will not send them and you will not see them from others either.
settings.commandsHint: Type these into the chat box. Reset brings the phone back to the middle of your screen if you ever move it out of view.
settings.commandMarket: Open the market board, optionally searching an item
settings.commandReset: Move the phone back to the center of the screen
settings.translateIntoHint: Posts, comments, and messages written in other languages get a one-tap Translate link that renders them in this language.
settings.autoTranslateHint: Posts and comments written in other languages are translated as soon as they appear, without tapping Translate. Private messages keep their own per-chat switch.

translate.chatOn: New messages in this chat are translated for you
translate.disclosureBody: Translations are made by Aethernet. Only the text you translate is sent. Private messages are never stored.
changelog.r0999.0: Added seven phone cases: Atomos, Baby Bat, Dwarf Rabbit, Enkidu, Horror, Kupo, and Runic, contributed by Remi and Silkie
changelog.r0999.1: Every phone case was recompressed, so the plugin downloads at less than half its old size even with the seven new cases
changelog.r0999.2: A message now appears in an open conversation the moment it arrives, instead of waiting for the next refresh
changelog.r0999.3: Opening a conversation, or coming back to one you left open, now pulls the newest messages straight away
changelog.r0999.4: Chat now says when it cannot reach the server and offers a retry, instead of quietly showing an old transcript
changelog.r0999.5: Landscape now runs the hardware buttons along the top and bottom edges and keeps the screen the size it has in portrait, contributed by Raya
changelog.r0999.6: Photo pickers now draw only the thumbnails you can see, so opening one with a large library no longer stalls, contributed by BluntEXE
changelog.r0999.7: A shortcut icon borrowed from another plugin now fills the tile all the way to its rounded edge
changelog.r0999.8: Housing filter chips no longer wrap their labels, and the filter drawer rows sit on the standard spacing, contributed by Chaosvanguard
changelog.r0999.9: Fixed one refused request pausing all the others: an upload stopped by the request limit no longer holds back sends and refreshes
changelog.r0999.10: Fixed the Doman Enclave daily reporting your whole allowance as outstanding, ignoring what you had already donated, contributed by Farroness
changelog.r0999.11: Fixed the venue website link falling back to a page that does not exist on FFXIV Venues, contributed by Raya
changelog.r0999.12: Fixed the case artwork rotating the wrong way in landscape and leaving a hairline gap along the edge of the phone, contributed by Raya
changelog.r0999.13: Fixed the German wording for the physical ranged role, two game names, and a Dailies tour card, contributed by Silkie
changelog.r0999.14: Home folders now hold shortcuts as well as apps, so a plugin launcher can be dragged in and grouped like any other icon, contributed by K.I.R.O
changelog.r0998.0: Added Housing, a new app that browses every housing ward on a map, tracks the plots you are watching, and reminds you before a lottery entry period closes, contributed by Chaosvanguard
changelog.r0998.1: Added Community Radio to Music, with more details coming soon
changelog.r0998.2: Added new phone cases, contributed by Silkie, Zivyl, Remi, and Rania
changelog.r0998.3: Badges have been completely reworked: they are now granted or earned under certain conditions, with the details on the Discord server
changelog.r0998.4: A fullscreen photo can be popped out into an ordinary window with a title bar, resized freely, and named after the app it came from
changelog.r0998.5: A photo can be filed into an album from the viewer, without leaving for the album first
changelog.r0998.6: The market now shows what lands in your retainer after tax, and names the city with the lowest rate
changelog.r0998.7: When another world, data center, or region sells an item cheaper, the Prices card names it and its price
changelog.r0998.8: An item that only sells HQ now opens on the HQ tab instead of an empty NQ one
changelog.r0998.9: Hovering a market row reveals the full item name, so families such as Ballroom Etiquette are no longer indistinguishable
changelog.r0998.10: Calls gained a Speaker picker, so a call plays through the output device you choose instead of always following the system default
changelog.r0998.11: Quiet While Busy holds banners, sounds, and shakes during combat, duties, cutscenes, and zoning; the notification still arrives and still counts as unread
changelog.r0998.12: Notification toasts can be turned off globally or per app, contributed by Radvo
changelog.r0998.13: An alarm whose minute passed while the plugin was unloaded now still fires, within a ten minute catch-up window
changelog.r0998.14: Every chat app now keeps a draft per conversation, so what you wrote for one person no longer follows you into the next
changelog.r0998.15: Velvet can pass on a profile, which drops them for the session without blocking them
changelog.r0998.16: Leaving the Velvet profile editor with unsaved changes now asks before discarding them
changelog.r0998.17: A Velvet profile you have already reported no longer offers the flag again
changelog.r0998.18: Dragging an icon past the last Home Screen page now opens a new page
changelog.r0998.19: Escape now backs out of the topmost thing on screen: a confirmation, the report sheet, the share sheet, then Control Center
changelog.r0998.20: Control Center can be pulled open by dragging the status band down, not only by tapping it
changelog.r0998.21: The community rules unlock their accept button once you have read to the end, instead of after a fixed countdown
changelog.r0998.22: Dock icons now raise the same name pill as the rest of the Home Screen
changelog.r0998.23: Removing an app from the Home Screen now asks first
changelog.r0998.24: Dalamud's settings button beside the plugin now opens the phone on the Settings app
changelog.r0998.25: A shortcut can use any plugin's icon, picked from the appearance sheet
changelog.r0998.26: Copying a chat bubble, a Linkpearl line, or a travel command now shows a confirmation, so a copy is no longer silent
changelog.r0998.27: An album's rename and delete are now reachable from a menu button on the card, not only by right-click
changelog.r0998.28: Empty screens now offer the next step: an empty photo library offers Camera, and Velvet offers Clear filters when your own filters are hiding everyone
changelog.r0998.29: A list that failed to load now says so and offers Retry, instead of reading as an empty list
changelog.r0998.30: Camera remembers the grid and the flash, and Photos reopens on the tab you left
changelog.r0998.31: The emoji picker takes the caret when it opens, so you can type to search instead of hunting the grid
changelog.r0998.32: Games that run on a clock now show a Paused veil when the phone loses focus, instead of looking frozen
changelog.r0998.33: The battery icon warns as a whole below twenty percent and breathes below ten, rather than tinting the fill alone
changelog.r0998.34: An empty inbox now offers New message instead of only describing itself
changelog.r0998.35: About gained a Copy Support Info row that puts versions, OS, language, and sound state on the clipboard, carrying no account or character identifiers
changelog.r0998.36: Fixed encryption and imported WAV and MP3 playback on Linux and Wine, contributed by Ehno
changelog.r0998.37: Fixed a message the game rejects disappearing in silence: the text stays in the box and the phone says the send failed
changelog.r0998.38: Fixed the housing translations: every language now uses the wording its own game client uses, and district names are translated
changelog.r0998.39: Fixed the calendar starting its week on Sunday in the five languages whose week starts on Monday
changelog.r0998.40: Fixed mini-games running on while the phone was not focused, and Tetris and Sudoku taking the keyboard while you were typing in the game
changelog.r0998.41: Fixed Settings showing badges you no longer hold
changelog.r0998.42: Fixed screens collapsing onto the avatar while a profile photo had not loaded yet, most visibly in the Velvet profile editor
changelog.r0998.43: Fixed the photo viewer's buttons stacking up over the photo
changelog.r0998.44: Fixed the Yellow Pages ad form cutting off its failure message instead of wrapping it, contributed by Raya
changelog.r0998.45: Moved the Velvet photo gallery below the profile details, contributed by Farroness
changelog.r0998.46: Fixed the emote idle scroll firing while an event window was open, contributed by Chaosvanguard
changelog.r0998.47: Fixed Escape doing nothing when the phone had been opened with a slash command
changelog.r0998.48: Fixed the app badge counting the conversation you are currently reading
changelog.r0998.49: Fixed blocking someone in Velvet leaving them in the Discover deck
changelog.r0998.50: Fixed Block on a Velvet profile acting without asking first
changelog.r0998.51: Fixed a blocking moderation notice vanishing for good once dismissed: it now leaves a notification behind
changelog.r0998.52: Fixed two notification settings showing in English in every translated language
changelog.r0998.53: Notifications no longer appear at the title screen, where there is no session to act on them
changelog.r0997.0: Added Shortcuts, a new app that turns a run of commands into a single tap and pins it to the home screen
changelog.r0997.1: You can now resize the phone by dragging the bottom right corner of its frame
changelog.r0997.2: Phone Size in Settings is a slider now, so you can pick any size instead of six fixed ones
changelog.r0997.3: The whole screen scales with the phone, so text and icons grow with it instead of staying small
changelog.r0997.4: Text Size is a slider too now, and it goes down to 70 percent for people who want smaller text
changelog.r0997.5: Accent is a full color picker now, so you can use any color you like instead of the five presets
changelog.r0997.6: Ringtone volume and notification volume are sliders now, so you can pick any level instead of four fixed steps
changelog.r0997.7: The minimized phone now stays the same size whatever size the phone itself is
changelog.r0997.8: Fixed notifications coming back after you cleared them, and badges staying lit after everything had been read
changelog.r0997.9: Fixed taps in the Control Center doing nothing while a menu or picker was open in the app behind it
changelog.r0996.0: You can now link your Patreon account from the account section in Settings
changelog.r0996.1: Linking grants your member perks automatically, including the Patreon member badge, and they follow your membership as it changes
changelog.r0996.2: Settings shows whether your membership is active once linked, and you can unlink Patreon at any time
changelog.r0995.0: The phone has a new body: a machined metal frame and a glass band, with one curve shared by the screen, the glass, and every case
changelog.r0995.1: Cases are now hand-painted art instead of flat tints, starting with Titanium and Silkie; the Silkie design was made by Nui
changelog.r0995.2: Case art can spill past the edge of the phone, and it stays visible while the phone is minimized
changelog.r0995.3: The phone now ships with its own ringtones and notification sounds, and calls and notifications each pick from their own library

encryption.title: Encrypted Chats
encryption.intro: End-to-end encryption keeps your chats between you and the people you write to. Not even the Aethernet server can read them.
encryption.notSignedIn: Sign in to your Aethernet account first.
encryption.unsupportedBody: This computer cannot create the security key that encrypted chats need, so Messages and Velvet chats stay unavailable here. This usually happens when the game runs through Wine or Proton. The rest of Aetherphone works normally.
encryption.unsupportedSummary: This PC cannot set up encryption, so messages here are not encrypted.

encryption.lockedBody: This device doesn't have the encryption key for this account, so messages here can't be read yet. This usually happens after switching to a different computer. Your messages are safe: open Aetherphone on the computer that already has your key, or create a new key here. If you create a new key, older messages become readable again once your chat partners come online.

encryption.lockedNoRecoveryBody: This device doesn't hold an encryption key for this account, and no recovery code was set up, so the old key can't be restored here. Create a new key anyway: everyone you talk to still holds the key to the chats you share, and their phone hands it to your new key the next time they open Aetherphone. Only a chat where everyone lost their key stays closed.
encryption.forgotNoRecoveryBody: A new key will be created. The key it replaces stays on this PC, so older messages keep opening here, and the people you chat with hand the key to your shared chats back to the new one when they next open Aetherphone. Save a recovery code afterwards so this PC is never the only way in.

encryption.recoveryNudgeBanner: Protect your chat history: set up a recovery code

encryption.recoveryConfiguredBody: A recovery code is set up for this account. Keep it somewhere safe: it's what unlocks your chats on another PC.
encryption.recoverySaveBody: This is the only way to restore your chats on another PC, and it can't be shown again. Keep it somewhere safe and private: anyone with this code can read your chats.
encryption.recoveryWrongCode: That code didn't work. Check it and try again.
encryption.recoveryOlderCode: That code is from before your key changed, so it can't unlock current chats, but the older chats it protects were unlocked on this PC. To unlock everything, use your newest code, your other PC, or create a new key.
encryption.recoveryKeyChanged: Your encryption key changed on another device, so this device can't create a recovery code right now. Wait a moment for this device to update, then try again.
encryption.restoreOlderBody: Keys replaced on this PC are tried automatically, and the people you chat with hand their copy of the conversation key back to your new key the next time they open Aetherphone. Messages sealed to a key that was never here can also be unlocked with the recovery code you had at the time.

encryption.forgotBody: A new key will be created. Keep your current recovery code: it is what opens your older messages on another PC.
encryption.olderKeyBanner: Some messages here were sent to an earlier key. They unlock when the other person next opens Aetherphone. Tap for details.
encryption.linkBody: If Aetherphone still works on your other computer, it can unlock this one for you. No code to type, and your full history comes with it.

encryption.helpOpen: What to do if chats stop opening
encryption.helpIntro: Your messages are stored on the server and never deleted. What can go missing is the key on this PC that opens them, so almost every case below is fixable.
encryption.helpDecryptingBody: Nothing is wrong. The keys for that chat are still loading and the messages appear within a few seconds. If it stays like this, reopen the phone.
encryption.helpLockedTitle: It says Locked on this device
encryption.helpLockedBody: This PC does not hold your key. If your other computer still works, use Unlock from my other PC above and approve it there: that is instant and brings everything. Otherwise enter your recovery code. If you have neither, create a new key: the people you chat with hand the key to your shared conversations back to it when they next open Aetherphone, and those chats open again.
encryption.helpOlderKeyTitle: It says Sent to an earlier key
encryption.helpOlderKeyBody: Those messages were written before your key changed. Keys replaced on this PC are tried automatically, and everyone you chat with still holds the conversation key: their phone hands it back to your new key the next time they open Aetherphone, so most of these clear on their own with nothing for you to do. A chat that stays locked means that person has not been online since your key changed, or lost their own key too. The recovery code you had at the time still opens it: see Older chats below.
encryption.helpUnreadableTitle: Windows will not open the key
encryption.helpUnreadableBody: The key is still saved here, Windows just refuses to open it. This happens when the game runs as a different Windows user, as administrator when it usually is not, or after Windows was reinstalled. Start the game the way you normally do and it should unlock itself.
encryption.helpDamagedTitle: It says This message is damaged
encryption.helpDamagedBody: That single message did not arrive intact. It cannot be repaired, but it does not affect the rest of the chat or your key.
encryption.helpNeverBody: Unlocking from another PC is the best route: it is instant and brings everything back. A recovery code is next. A new key comes last, but it is no longer a dead end: this PC keeps the key it replaces, and everyone you chat with hands back the key to each conversation you share once they open Aetherphone again. The one thing a new key cannot bring back is a chat where every other person lost their key too.
encryption.helpPreventBody: Keep a recovery code saved, and keep every code you have ever generated: each one opens only the key it was made for. This PC also holds on to the keys it replaces, the people you chat with hand their copy of a shared conversation key back to whatever key you have now, and messages you have already read stay readable even if the key is lost. A code is still worth keeping: it is what works when nobody else is around to hand a key back.

encryption.unreadableKeyBody: Windows could not open the encryption key saved on this PC. This usually means the game is running as a different Windows user, or Windows was reinstalled. Your key is still here and untouched: start the game the way you normally do and it should unlock. Try that before creating a new key, since nothing has actually been lost.

onboarding.allInOneBody: Chat, music, weather, the market board, mini-games and more, all in your pocket.
onboarding.widgetTourBody: Widgets live on your Home Screen and update on their own. This one shows the Eorzean weather wherever you're standing.
onboarding.customizeBody: Press and hold anywhere on the Home Screen to rearrange icons, resize widgets, and add new ones.
onboarding.homeTourBody: Your phone is ready. Before you dive in, here's a quick look around.
onboarding.appsTourBody: Tap any icon to open an app. The bar at the bottom of the screen always brings you back home.
onboarding.controlCenterTapBody: Tap the top of the screen to open Control Center.
onboarding.controlCenterInsideBody: Volume, brightness, accent color and your notifications all live here. Tap the bottom edge to close it anytime; for now, Continue will do it for you.
onboarding.signalTourBody: These bars are your real ping to Aethernet, updating as you play. More bars means a faster connection.
onboarding.batteryTourBody: And this is your device's actual battery, read straight from your computer.
onboarding.minimizeBody: This side button shrinks the phone into a small one in the corner that keeps showing the time, your music and new alerts. Tap it to bring the phone back, or hold it to turn off.
onboarding.lockBody: This button locks the phone's position on your screen so it stays put while you play. That's the tour: enjoy your Aetherphone.
onboarding.messagesBody: Every /tell you get in game turns into a chat bubble here. Read and reply straight from your phone, and get a badge the moment someone new writes.
onboarding.skywatcherBody: Live Eorzean weather for wherever you're standing, refreshed as you travel.
onboarding.skywatcherForecastBody: And here's what's coming, hour by hour, so you can plan around the weather.
onboarding.marketBody: Live market board prices from across your world, powered by Universalis. Search any item, or right-click one in game to look it up.
onboarding.marketStatsBody: See the cheapest listings, price history and sale trends, and set an alert to get pinged when a price drops.
onboarding.venuesBody: Discover live player-run venues and events, from clubs to photo spots. One tap travels you there with Lifestream.
onboarding.musicBody: Your in-game music player. Browse genre radio stations or search for any track you like.
onboarding.musicNowPlayingBody: Playback keeps going while you play, with a Now Playing banner right on your home screen.
onboarding.gamesBody: A whole pocket arcade, 15 mini-games from puzzles to reflex tests, and every one remembers your best score.
onboarding.cameraBody: Snap in-game photos straight from your phone. Pick square or photo, frame up with the grid, and tap the shutter.
onboarding.photosBody: Every shot you take lands here in a tidy gallery. Tap any photo to view it full-screen.
onboarding.settingsBody: Themes, wallpapers, text size and how your phone behaves. Poke around and set it up just how you like.
onboarding.contactsBody: Your in-game friends, laid out like a proper address book with their portraits. Tap anyone to start a conversation.
onboarding.characterBody: Your day in Eorzea at a glance: three rings that fill as you play and reset at midnight.
onboarding.chirperBody: Welcome to Chirper! A little social feed built just for the Aetherphone community, short posts and timelines with other players.
onboarding.chirperPostBody: Post what's on your mind, follow people, and reply or react to their chirps. It runs on our own network, completely separate from the Lodestone.
onboarding.chirperKindBody: This space is for everyone. Discriminatory, hateful or harmful content isn't welcome and can get you banned.
onboarding.aethergramBody: Welcome to Aethergram! A photo-sharing app made for the Aetherphone community, a lot like the real thing.
onboarding.aethergramShareBody: Set up your profile, post your best shots, follow other players, and like or comment on theirs.
onboarding.aethergramSafeBody: It's completely separate from the Lodestone. Nothing here is linked to your character or account.
onboarding.aethergramKindBody: This space is for everyone. Discriminatory, hateful or harmful content isn't welcome and can get you banned.
onboarding.mapsBody: Every zone map with its aetherytes and points of interest. Star the places you visit most for one-tap access.
onboarding.findPeopleBody: Look up any character or Free Company on the Lodestone, profiles, gear and rosters, right from your phone.
onboarding.newsBody: The Lodestone feed for your region, topics, notices, maintenance times and updates, with a tap to read the full story.
onboarding.collectionsBody: Track your mounts, minions, emotes, orchestrion rolls and more. See what you've got and what's still out there to find.
onboarding.walletBody: Gil, tomestones, hunt seals and every currency you care about, with your weekly caps, all at a glance.
onboarding.inventoryBody: Peek at what's on you and stashed with your retainers, so you always know what you're carrying.
onboarding.timersBody: Countdowns to the daily, Grand Company and weekly resets, plus Fashion Report, the Jumbo Cactpot and your retainer ventures. Switch on reminders and the phone nudges you.
onboarding.dailiesBody: A simple checklist for your daily and weekly routines. Tick things off and it all resets right on schedule.
onboarding.fishingBody: Bite windows, handy tips and the best spots for the fish worth chasing.
onboarding.notificationsBody: A running history of everything your phone has pinged you about, so nothing slips past you.
onboarding.velvetDiscoverBody: Browse profiles filtered by what people are looking for, and send a connection request when you find someone interesting.
onboarding.velvetFilterBody: Narrow the people here to exactly what you want, from ERP to gpose to just making friends.
onboarding.velvetFeedBody: This is the live feed, where people share photos and posts across Velvet. Everything here stays inside Velvet.
onboarding.velvetActivityBody: Likes, comments and new intros land here. Tap the bell any time to catch up.
onboarding.velvetMessagesBody: Accept or decline requests, then chat privately with the connections you make.
onboarding.velvetProfileBody: Set up your intro, vibe, tags and limits, and choose whether you're discoverable to others.
onboarding.velvetKindBody: This space is for everyone. Discriminatory, hateful or harmful content isn't welcome and can get you banned.
onboarding.feedbackIntroBody: Tell the developer what you think: suggestions, bug reports, feature ideas, or just a hello.
onboarding.feedbackWriteBody: Type your message and tap Send. Your feedback goes directly to the developer's dashboard.
onboarding.feedbackPrivacyBody: Your character name is attached so the developer knows who you are in game. Be constructive and kind.
onboarding.messageBody: Message and call your friends in one place. Add friends by number in Contacts, chat in Chats, and talk over voice from Calls.
onboarding.phoneBody: Call your friends directly in-game and talk over voice chat. The other person needs the Aetherphone plugin too, and you both need to be signed in to Aethernet from Settings.
onboarding.phoneGroupBody: While a call is active, add more people to bring everyone into the same conversation. Group calls are supported too.
onboarding.phoneVoiceBody: You can pick your microphone and adjust voice input options from Settings.
onboarding.calendarBody: A month view of community events across Eorzea, right beside your own plans. Tap any day to see what's on.
onboarding.calendarAddBody: Tap the plus to save your own event with its date and time. It sits on the calendar alongside everything else.
onboarding.notesBody: A quick place to jot things down. Tap the plus to start a note, and it saves itself as you type.
onboarding.notesRemindersBody: Switch to the Reminders tab for a simple to-do list. Give one a due date and the phone nudges you when it's time.
onboarding.calculatorBody: A simple calculator for quick everyday sums, with a running tape of your recent results to scroll back through.
onboarding.pollsBody: Community polls from across Aethernet. Tap an option to cast your vote and see where everyone stands.
onboarding.pollsResultsBody: Every vote updates the bars in real time. Once a poll closes, you'll see the final tally.
onboarding.chirperTabsBody: For You shows chirps from everyone; Following keeps it to the people you follow. Swap between them any time.
onboarding.chirperSearchBody: Search for other players by name or handle, and follow them to build your Following feed.
onboarding.chirperActivityBody: Likes, replies and new followers all land under the bell.
onboarding.aethergramSearchBody: Tap Search to look up other players, browse their grids, and follow the ones you like.
onboarding.aethergramActivityBody: Hearts, comments and new followers show up under this tab the moment they happen.
onboarding.aethergramProfileBody: Tap your avatar to set up your profile and watch your grid fill up with your shots.
onboarding.velvetComposeBody: Post thoughts and photos for your connections. Everything you share stays inside Velvet.
onboarding.messageContactsBody: Friends you add by number live in Contacts. Tap the tab to take a look.
onboarding.messageNumberCopyBody: This card is your number. Tap it to copy, then share it in game so friends can add you.
onboarding.messageAddFriendBody: Got someone's number? Tap the plus and their card appears right here.
onboarding.musicSearchBody: Type a song or artist and the results stream straight to your phone.
onboarding.musicRadioBody: Pick a genre to browse live radio stations. Tap one and it starts playing instantly.
onboarding.marketSearchBody: Type a couple of letters to search every marketable item, or look one up straight from the game.
onboarding.marketScopeBody: Compare prices on your world, your data center, or the whole region. Your pick is remembered.
onboarding.venuesTimeBody: Filter events by when they happen: live right now, today, upcoming, or everything.
onboarding.venuesFilterBody: Tap a chip to filter by data center, source, tags, or just your favorites.
onboarding.venuesSearchBody: Know the name? Search venues and events directly here.
onboarding.gamesFeaturedBody: A different game is featured every day. Tap the card to jump straight in.
onboarding.gamesLibraryBody: Every game sorted by genre, with your best score under each title.
onboarding.cameraModesBody: Square gives a centered crop, Photo uses the full viewfinder.
onboarding.cameraFlashBody: With the flash on, the screen blinks white as you capture. Handy in dark zones.
onboarding.cameraShutterBody: Tap the shutter to snap what's behind the phone. Shots land straight in the Photos app.
onboarding.photosEmptyBody: Photos come from the Camera app. Take a shot and it appears in this grid instantly.
onboarding.notesNewBody: Tap the plus to open a fresh note. It saves itself as you type.
onboarding.notesReminderBody: On this tab the plus creates a reminder. Give it a due date and the phone nudges you.
onboarding.calendarAgendaBody: Whatever day you pick, its events line up here, community happenings beside your own plans.
onboarding.settingsAccountBody: Sign in here to unlock the social side of the phone: Chirper, Aethergram, Polls and more.
onboarding.settingsAppearanceBody: Theme, accent color and wallpaper all live in Appearance. Make the phone yours.
onboarding.settingsTutorialsBody: Replay any tour or turn tips off entirely from Tutorials.
onboarding.notificationsHistoryBody: Everything the phone pinged you about stacks up here. Tap one to jump to its app, or clear them all up top.
onboarding.messagesListBody: Every /tell becomes a conversation here. Tap one to read and reply without leaving the game.
onboarding.messagesLinkshellsBody: Build a tab from the channels you actually read, like your free company or your linkshells, and only those land here.
onboarding.feedbackSendBody: When you're happy with it, tap Send. It goes straight to the developer's dashboard.
onboarding.pollsVoteBody: Each card is one community poll. Tap an option to vote. You can switch your pick while it's open.
onboarding.skywatcherCurrentBody: This is the zone you're standing in and its live weather, refreshed as you travel.
onboarding.mapsLocationBody: Maps always knows where you're standing. Your current zone and region sit right at the top.
onboarding.mapsSearchBody: Type a zone or aetheryte name to jump straight to it. With Lifestream installed, one tap travels there.
onboarding.mapsStarBody: Expand an expansion, then tap the star beside any destination to pin it to your Favorites.
onboarding.findPeopleSearchBody: Type a character's name here. The world field is set to your data center, but you can point it anywhere.
onboarding.findPeopleKindBody: Flip this to look up Free Companies instead, with crests, slogans and full member rosters.
onboarding.newsCategoriesBody: Topics, notices, maintenance windows and patch updates, each on its own tab.
onboarding.newsReadBody: Tap any card or row to open the full article in your browser.
onboarding.newsRefreshBody: News refreshes on its own, but a tap here pulls the latest right now.
onboarding.contactsListBody: Your friend list, online first, with portraits. Tap anyone for actions like messaging and party invites.
onboarding.contactsSearchBody: Start typing a name to filter the list instantly.
onboarding.characterRingsBody: Progress tracks experience, Adventure counts duties, and Fortune counts gil earned today. Play to close all three.
onboarding.characterSummaryBody: Today's totals in detail: experience, duties, gil, playtime and new collectibles, with your current session below.
onboarding.clockIntroBody: Eorzea time, server time and your own cities, ticking side by side. And that's just the first tab.
onboarding.clockTabsBody: Alarms, a stopwatch and a timer live behind these tabs. Tap here to try the alarms.
onboarding.clockAddBody: This plus creates a new alarm here, or adds a city on the World tab.
onboarding.calculatorTapeBody: Past results pile up here as you calculate. Tap any old result to drop it into a new sum.
onboarding.timersResetsBody: Daily, Grand Company and weekly resets counted down live, each with the time it lands for you.
onboarding.timersRemindersBody: Flip a toggle and the phone pings you when that reset hits or a retainer venture finishes.
onboarding.dailiesCadenceBody: Your routines split into Daily and Weekly. Tap here to flip over to the weekly list.
onboarding.dailiesBadgeBody: The Home icon counts what is still unfinished. Turn it off and the app stays quiet until you open it.
onboarding.fishingHeroBody: This card is your next boarding window, with the route, its time of day and a countdown to departure.
onboarding.fishingBlueBody: The rare blue fish catchable on this route, each with the bait that tempts it.
onboarding.fishingUpcomingBody: Boats leave every two hours. Scroll the schedule to find a departure that suits you.
onboarding.walletGilBody: Your live gil balance, refreshed as you earn and spend.
onboarding.walletCurrenciesBody: Tomestones, seals and scrip grouped by family. Capped currencies show a bar so you know when to spend.
onboarding.inventorySearchBody: Type an item name to search your bags, saddlebag, retainers and FC chest all at once.
onboarding.inventorySummaryBody: How much you're carrying and your gil, front and center.
onboarding.inventorySourcesBody: Open a retainer or the FC chest once and the phone keeps a snapshot here, browsable any time.
onboarding.collectionsCategoryBody: Each tile is a collection with your completion ring. Tap Mounts to open its catalog.
onboarding.collectionsSearchBody: Search the whole catalog by name, or filter by where it comes from.
onboarding.collectionsMissingBody: With your Lodestone linked, flip to Missing to see exactly what's left to hunt down.
onboarding.storeTourBody: The phone starts with a handful of apps. The App Store has the rest, and you decide which ones live on your Home Screen.
onboarding.appStoreBody: Every app on the phone comes from here. Install what you want, skip what you don't, and come back whenever you change your mind.
onboarding.appStoreGetBody: Tap Get to add an app to your Home Screen, or tap the row itself to read what it does first.
onboarding.appStoreBrowseBody: Apps groups everything by what it's for: social, utilities, games and more.
onboarding.appStoreSearchBody: Search finds an app by name in one go.
onboarding.appStoreRemoveBody: Press and hold an icon on the Home Screen to remove an app. Your data stays put, and you can install it again from here.
onboarding.jobsBody: Every gearset you own, grouped by role, with the one you're wearing marked as active.
onboarding.jobsSwitchBody: Tap any row to equip that gearset. Crafters and gatherers switch the same way.
onboarding.jobsCategoriesBody: Build custom categories to keep raid sets, crafters or alt jobs together, in whatever order suits you.
onboarding.jobsColorBody: The palette recolors the app. Choose a preset or mix your own and save it.
onboarding.musterBody: Player meetups happening right now across the data centers. Find one, say you're coming, and travel over.
onboarding.musterScopeBody: Narrow the list to your data center or open it up to the whole region. The globe pins any data center you like.
onboarding.musterCategoriesBody: Filter by what's happening: hangouts, hunts, raids, roleplay and the rest.
onboarding.musterStartBody: Set a place, a time and how many can come, and your meetup shows up for everyone else.
onboarding.musterSafetyBody: Hosts only see who you are once you say you're coming. Keep it welcoming, and report anything that isn't.
onboarding.yellowPagesBody: Player classifieds: shops, services, venues and hires, all posted by other players.
onboarding.yellowPagesScopeBody: Ads are filtered to your region by default. Widen or narrow that here.
onboarding.yellowPagesSearchBody: Type what you need, or use the category tiles underneath to jump straight to a section.
onboarding.yellowPagesPostBody: Write it, add photos and opening hours, and it stays up until it expires. You can edit or renew it any time.
onboarding.yellowPagesInquiriesBody: When someone asks about an ad, the conversation opens in Inquiries, encrypted end to end.
onboarding.yellowPagesSafetyBody: Nobody vets these ads. Agree on the gil up front, meet in game, and report anything that smells like a scam.
onboarding.announcementsBody: News straight from the Aetherphone team: releases, downtime and anything else worth knowing.
onboarding.announcementsCardBody: The newest post sits on top. Tap it for the full story; anything you haven't read is highlighted.
onboarding.announcementsQuietBody: Announcements always stays on the phone, but you can turn its notifications off in Settings.
onboarding.healthBody: Your character's activity: every yalm walked, swum and flown, counted while you play.
onboarding.healthTodayBody: Steps against your daily goal, with active time, energy and hydration right underneath.
onboarding.healthTabsBody: Activity, water, goals, history and your profile each get a tab. Tap Goals to set your own targets.
onboarding.healthGoalsBody: Switch a goal on and it appears on the overview with a progress bar and your streak.
onboarding.healthPrivacyBody: None of this is uploaded anywhere. It's tracked per character and saved with your phone.
onboarding.coinBody: Aether Coin is the phone's own currency. You earn it simply by using the phone, and it stacks up quietly while you go about your day.
onboarding.coinBalanceBody: Your balance up top, with what you earned today and your all-time totals underneath.
onboarding.coinCheckInBody: Check in once a day for coin. The streak bonus grows the longer you keep it going, and one missed day a week is forgiven.
onboarding.coinEarnBody: Calls, conversations, games and posts all pay out. Each row shows what you've earned against its cap for the period.
onboarding.coinShopBody: The shop is where your coin goes. It's still filling out, so check back as new things land.
onboarding.coinFairBody: Coin can't be bought with real money, and it never buys an advantage. You can also earn it at community events and across the phone's other apps.
onboarding.shortcutsBody: Chain the commands you type every day into a single tap: emote routines, travel, opening your other plugins.
onboarding.shortcutsNewBody: Stack steps in order: game commands, waits between them, a plugin to open or a link to launch.
onboarding.shortcutsLibraryBody: A tap on the row runs the whole chain and reports each step as it goes. The sliders on the right open it for editing.
onboarding.shortcutsImportBody: Shortcuts copy out as plain text, so you can send one to a friend and import theirs straight back in.
onboarding.shortcutsPluginsBody: The Plugins tab lists what's installed and every command it registers, ready to drop into a shortcut.
onboarding.shortcutsHomeBody: Any shortcut can sit on the home screen as its own tile, with an icon and color you choose.
onboarding.housingBody: Open plots across every world, with lottery timers, so you know where to be and when.
onboarding.housingContextBody: World, district and ward. Change any of the three and the map follows.
onboarding.housingMapBody: Every marker is a plot, sized small to large. Drag to pan, scroll to zoom, and tap one for its price and lottery details.
onboarding.housingPhaseBody: Entry or results, and how long is left on the one closing soonest. It counts down live.
onboarding.housingFiltersBody: Filter by size, phase, private or Free Company, even how many entries are already in. A crowded ward becomes the few worth chasing.
onboarding.housingWatchBody: Watch a plot and the phone reminds you before its phase ends, with however much warning you ask for.
onboarding.housingDataBody: Listings come from community scans, so the chip in the footer tells you how recent they are. Refresh beside it pulls again.
onboarding.casinoBody: The phone's own casino floor. You play with chips bought using Aether Coin, so nothing here costs real money and nothing here buys an advantage.
onboarding.casinoChipsBody: Chips on the left, your coin on the right. Buy in at 100 chips per coin, and cash out whatever you're holding whenever you like.
onboarding.casinoSpinBody: One spin on the house each day, no chips needed. Take it and come back tomorrow for the next one.
onboarding.casinoFloorBody: Blackjack, slots, scratch cards, bingo, the wheel and a round with the barkeep. Tap one to sit down, or open Games to read the rules and payouts first.
onboarding.casinoRecordsBody: Every stake and payout goes on the record. Fair play goes further: each round is sealed before you tap, revealed when it settles, and re-checked right here on your phone.
onboarding.casinoLimitsBody: Cap what you can lose in a day and the floor holds you to it. Lowering it takes effect at once, raising it waits, so the choice is the one you made while calm.
onboarding.casinoLiveBody: Gamba is not a solo affair. Tap Live for the rooms and tables that have people in them right now.
onboarding.casinoRoomsBody: The wheel and the bingo hall run on a shared timer, so everyone plays the same round together. Blackjack seats you at a table with real players.
onboarding.aetherStreamBody: Video inside the game. Paste a link and it plays here on your phone, or on a screen you place out in the world.
onboarding.aetherStreamPlayerBody: Whatever is playing shows up here. Once you cast it into the world, a live badge appears in the corner along with everyone watching with you.
onboarding.aetherStreamAddBody: A YouTube link, a direct video URL, or a file from your own machine. Play Now starts it straight away, Add to Queue lines it up behind what's running.
onboarding.aetherStreamTransportBody: Play and pause, jump ten seconds either way, or skip to whatever is next. Drag the bar above to scrub, and the dial below sets the volume.
onboarding.aetherStreamActionsBody: Up Next holds your queue, Party is for watching with other people, and Screen puts the picture onto a surface in the world.
onboarding.aetherStreamPartyBody: Start a party and players nearby can ask to join. You decide who comes in, and everyone stays on the same second of the same video.
onboarding.aetherStreamSettingsBody: Maximum quality, hardware decoding, whether others can find your stream, and the components the player needs, all behind this cog.
onboarding.huntsBody: A Faloop account is required for live spawn data. Browsing marks and mob info works without one. Faloop is not affiliated with Aetherphone.
onboarding.huntsSignInBody: Tap here to sign in or create a Faloop account and start getting live spawns.
onboarding.huntsGuideBody: Want to learn more about hunts? Check our guide for more information.
setup.welcomeBody: Your very own smartphone, right here in Eorzea. A few quick steps and it's ready to go.
setup.appearanceBody: Pick a light or dark look for your phone. Dynamic follows Eorzean time, so the phone turns dark after sunset.
setup.accountBody: One account unlocks every social app: Chirper, Aethergram, Message and more. Sign in with your character, no password needed.
setup.signedInBody: Signed in as {0}. Next, make your profile yours.
setup.idBody: Your Aethernet ID is how other players find you across Chirper, Aethergram and Message. Tap the circle to add a photo.
setup.handleRules: 3 to 15 characters: lowercase letters, numbers and underscores.
setup.handleTaken: That handle isn't available. Try another one.
setup.featureMessageBody: Chats, calls and contacts with players everywhere.
setup.featureSocialBody: Post on Chirper and Aethergram with one account.
setup.featureToolsBody: Market board, weather, maps, timers and news.
setup.featurePlayBody: Music, radio and a shelf of mini-games.
setup.readyBody: You're all set. Enjoy your Aetherphone.

conduct.yellowpages.allowed.1: Venue nights, game nights, and housing tours with honest schedules
conduct.yellowpages.allowed.2: Crafting, gathering, portraits, glamour, and performance work for gil
conduct.yellowpages.allowed.3: Recruiting for free companies, statics, and venue staff
conduct.yellowpages.allowed.5: Mod ads that show the work and link to the mod page: SFW mods only, no NSFW mods
conduct.yellowpages.allowed.6: Plugin ads only for modding and GPose plugins: QoL, UI, and automation are excluded
conduct.yellowpages.gil.title: Gil Only
conduct.yellowpages.gil.lead: Ads may only ask for gil. The following are never allowed:
conduct.yellowpages.gil.1: Real money, gift cards, or payments taken outside the game
conduct.yellowpages.gil.2: RMT, gil selling, account services, or third-party boosting shops
conduct.yellowpages.gil.3: Selling mods, plugins, or commissions for them: those ads link out and carry no price
conduct.yellowpages.honest.title: Honest Listings
conduct.yellowpages.honest.lead: An ad is a promise to whoever answers it. Do not post:
conduct.yellowpages.honest.1: Fake listings or services you cannot deliver
conduct.yellowpages.honest.2: Prices, schedules, or turnaround times you cannot honor
conduct.yellowpages.honest.3: Impersonating another venue, crafter, or free company
conduct.yellowpages.honest.4: Reposting the same ad to dodge the expiry cycle
conduct.yellowpages.honest.5: Ads left live once the work or event is over
conduct.yellowpages.appropriate.title: Keep It Appropriate
conduct.yellowpages.appropriate.lead: The After Dark tag marks mature venues and late-night events. It is not permission to post:
conduct.yellowpages.appropriate.2: ERP, escort, or sexual solicitation services
conduct.yellowpages.appropriate.4: Explicit language in titles, photos, or ad text
conduct.yellowpages.childSafety.title: Child Safety
conduct.yellowpages.childSafety.body: Any content involving or sexualizing child-like characters or minors is strictly prohibited, regardless of lore or stated age.
conduct.yellowpages.respect.title: Be Respectful
conduct.yellowpages.respect.lead: Treat others with respect. Do not engage in:
conduct.yellowpages.respect.4: Pressuring or badgering someone through inquiries
conduct.yellowpages.respect.5: Impersonation of real people or misinformation intended to deceive
conduct.yellowpages.spam.title: No Spam
conduct.yellowpages.spam.lead: Keep the board worth browsing. Do not post:
conduct.yellowpages.spam.2: Ads filed under unrelated categories or tags
conduct.yellowpages.privacy.title: Protect Privacy
conduct.yellowpages.privacy.body: Do not share another person's personal information, private conversations, or confidential content without their permission.
conduct.yellowpages.creators.title: Respect Creators
conduct.yellowpages.creators.lead: Only upload content you have the right to share. Do not:
conduct.yellowpages.creators.2: Remove watermarks or repost commissioned work without permission
conduct.yellowpages.creators.3: Claim someone else's creations as your own
conduct.yellowpages.discretion.title: Moderator Discretion
conduct.yellowpages.discretion.body: Ads that are misleading, off-topic, or otherwise inappropriate for a public board may be removed at moderator discretion.

changelog.r1006.0: Music and MogCast play songs again, after a change at YouTube left every track failing to load while search kept working
changelog.r1006.1: Photos sent in Velvet and the other chat apps no longer turn into a grey box after a while, and scrolling back to one no longer downloads it again
changelog.r1006.2: Chinese and Japanese now show every character, instead of leaving blank gaps where the text should be
changelog.r1006.3: Switching the phone's language now finishes in one short load, with the whole new alphabet ready straight away
changelog.r1007.0: The Aether Pot has been rebuilt: it now grows for days instead of hours, pays far bigger when it lands, and restarts from a funded reserve instead of zero. Every chip staked buys the same share of the draw, so small spins and big ones are priced alike
changelog.r1007.1: Bingo prizes are now sized to the hall: a quiet room pays the same fair return as a packed one, and a stage prize still always grows as more cards join
changelog.r1007.2: Round verification understands the pot's new draw, so fresh slots rounds check out end to end just like old ones
changelog.r1009.0: Added Hunts, an app that tracks hunt marks across your data center: see at a glance which spawn windows are open, capped or closed, filter by rank, world, status and expansion, and open a mark for its zone map, spawn condition, lore and rewards. One tap travels you there and plants the flag, a notification calls out a spawn the moment it goes up, and a built-in guide explains how the windows work. Live spawn data comes from Faloop and needs a free account, contributed by Deldee
changelog.r1009.1: Housing now covers the Chinese worlds: all four data centers and their worlds appear in the world picker under China, contributed by NiGuangOwO
changelog.r1009.2: The MogCast screen in the world shows up for players running DLSS, FSR or a lowered 3D resolution, instead of staying invisible until upscaling was switched off
changelog.r1009.3: MogCast picks a long video back up when the picture freezes or the sound drops out, and when a link will not play it says why in a plain sentence instead of showing raw error text
changelog.r1009.4: Dragging to scroll no longer snaps a list to one end when the same tap opens a new screen, or stalls when the drag passes over the Dynamic Island or a notification banner, contributed by Deldee
changelog.r1009.5: The notifications list in Settings is sorted by app name in your language, contributed by Deldee
changelog.r1010.0: Posts and comments written in another language now carry a Translate link in Chirper, Aethergram and Velvet: one tap swaps in the translation, a footer names the language it came from, and Show original brings the text back
changelog.r1010.1: Chats in ChocoChat, Aethergram and Velvet can translate a single message from its menu, and a Translate this chat switch in the thread header translates every new message as it arrives
changelog.r1010.2: Settings > Language picks the language you translate into, defaulting to your phone language. Translations are made by Aethernet, only the text you translate is sent, and private messages are never stored
changelog.r1010.3: A MogCast host can play a local file in a watch party without sharing its path: viewers are asked to locate their own copy, the phone checks it matches the host's, and playback runs in sync from there
changelog.r1010.4: Viewers in a MogCast watch party keep pace by speeding up or slowing down slightly instead of jumping on every host update, and only seek when they drift more than three seconds
changelog.r1010.5: When a MogCast video will not play, a card says so with Retry and, for the host, Skip: a stalled stream resumes from where it stopped, and the host sees how many viewers cannot play the current video
changelog.r1010.6: Added Skyfall to Games: tap the sky to send an interceptor that bursts and sweeps every meteor inside, and keep six settlements standing wave after wave
changelog.r1010.7: Added Invaders to Games: a rank marches down on your cannon and four bunkers, speeding up as it thins, with a saucer worth 300 crossing the top now and then
changelog.r1010.8: Added CapMan to Games: eat every dot in the maze, dodge four ghosts with habits of their own, and turn on them for a few seconds with a power pellet
changelog.r1010.9: Added Hop to Games: hop a critter across traffic and drifting pads to fill five dens before the timer runs out, with faster lanes every level
changelog.r1010.10: Added Squadron to Games: shoot ships that peel off their formation in dive runs, and free a fighter caught by a tractor beam to fly as a dual fighter
changelog.r1010.11: Tetris now steers with WASD as well as the arrows: A and D move, W rotates, S soft drops
changelog.r1010.12: Keys pressed in a game now stay in the game: the arrows in Tetris and Sudoku and WASD in the new games no longer walk your character
changelog.r1010.13: The Translate link also sits under profile bios and Velvet intros, Yellow Pages ads, Muster descriptions, Venues descriptions, and story captions
changelog.r1010.14: Settings > General gains Auto-translate posts and comments, which translates posts and comments in another language as soon as they appear, without tapping Translate; chats keep their own per-chat switch
changelog.r1010.15: Added Doom to Games: the real engine runs on the phone in fullscreen landscape, played on the keyboard with WASD, the arrows or a drag to turn, Space, E and 1 to 7
changelog.r1010.16: Added Word Run to Games: guess five-letter words one after another until one beats you, faster solves pay more, with word banks in five languages plus names from the game
changelog.r1010.17: Tetris gains a Modern ruleset beside Classic, with SRS kicks, lock delay, T-spins, back-to-back and combo scoring, and its own best score
changelog.r1015.0: Fixed an issue where pressing Previous, Next or Pause on the Dynamic Island's music card opened the Music app instead of controlling playback
changelog.r1014.0: Fixed Chirper no longer offering the Translate link on posts and replies written in another language
changelog.r1014.1: Tapping the reaction pill under a Chirper post now joins its reaction, and a pill holding several reactions expands into one chip per reaction so you can pick the one to add
changelog.r1014.2: Fixed the phone creeping away from its place after each turn to landscape and back, each orientation now remembers its own resting spot
changelog.r1014.3: Fixed Linkpearl pop-out menus staying open and out of reach after that window lost focus
changelog.r1014.4: The Gamba rules and Payouts sheets now explain the ten Slots paylines and how the house jackpot draw works
changelog.r1014.5: Fixed the Slots jackpot meter reading full long before the pot reached its 50,000 coin cap
changelog.r1014.6: Fixed long Slots banners and the jackpot hint clipping at the cabinet edge, they now glide across instead
changelog.r1014.7: The Slots reel window now shakes, flashes gold and runs a chase of marquee bulbs when the jackpot lands
changelog.r1014.8: Added three new phone cases: Emet-Selch, Bubbles and Warrior, contributed by mapleterra and kingzafar
changelog.r1014.9: Apps now answer taps while they are still opening, and a swipe on the home indicator mid-open sends them straight back instead of waiting for the animation to finish
changelog.r1014.10: Drag the home indicator upward to shrink an app with the cursor, then let go to close it or drop it back into place
changelog.r1014.11: The home screen icons now fade away while an app grows out of them, and the app's content only appears once its card is large enough to read
changelog.r1014.13: Improved app opening: the wallpaper now zooms and blurs behind the growing app card instead of only dimming
changelog.r1014.14: Fixed the Chirper Home, Explore, Activity and Profile tabs sharing one scroll position, each tab now keeps its own place
changelog.r1014.12: Who reacted to a Chirper post now lives under View reactions in the post's More menu
changelog.r1013.0: Redesigned Chirper around Home, Explore, Activity and Profile tabs, with edge to edge posts, threaded replies and a new compose pill
changelog.r1013.1: Chirper now shows profile pictures on posts, a banner on profiles, and which reaction each person left in the likers list
changelog.r1013.2: Chirper tabs now refresh when you come back to them, and name effects play everywhere in the app
changelog.r1013.3: Added search to the home screen: pull down on the app grid to find apps, settings, messages, notes and shortcuts, or do quick math
changelog.r1013.4: Apps now come back where you left them, keeping their tab, draft, screen and scroll
changelog.r1013.5: Apps now draw placeholder rows while their first page loads, instead of a spinner
changelog.r1013.6: Added MogCast, Music, News and Hunts to the Chinese game version
changelog.r1013.46: The Simplified Chinese translation has been polished across the phone, from app names to Eorzean units and the moderation wording, contributed by Nero0421
changelog.r1013.7: Mods has been taken out of the phone, browsing and installing Heliosphere mods happens in the Heliosphere plugin
changelog.r1013.8: Beat can now be played with the keyboard, on 1 to 4 or A, S, D and F
changelog.r1013.9: Added a Trademark document and refreshed the official Aetherphone documents in the GitHub repository

changelog.r1013.11: Chat pop-outs can now hide in combat and in duties, fade while you are away, and come back when you are free

casino.fairness.intro: Every game here is dealt from a sealed seed, and you can check any settled round yourself, right on this phone. Here is how it works.
casino.fairness.lockBody: Before a stake is accepted, Gamba publishes a fingerprint of the round's secret seed. The outcome is fixed in that seed; nothing after your tap can bend it.
casino.fairness.revealBody: When the round settles, the seed itself is revealed. Hash it and it must match the fingerprint published up front, bit for bit.
casino.fairness.replayBody: Your phone re-derives every draw the round logged from the revealed seed, and each one has to come out the same. The check runs here, not at the house.
casino.fairness.chainNote: Every round also carries the sealed fingerprint of the round after it, so the chain never breaks.

hunts.guideHowItWorksBody:
Each mark has a preset window it can spawn in after its last death. A spawn moment gets picked somewhere inside that window, and the mark can only spawn when its condition is met once that moment has passed.

By tracking these windows, along with when marks spawn and die, we can effectively track every S-rank across every world.

Note that for most marks this isn't random: a window shown at 60% means there's a 60% chance the mark is currently active, not a 60% chance that it will spawn.
hunts.guideRanksBody:
F-rank marks, often called FATE marks, come at the end of long FATE chains and only spawn every few hours or days.

B-rank marks are weekly hunt marks. They respawn 5 seconds after the last one is killed, so they're essentially always up.

A-rank marks are rare targets that respawn every few hours with no conditions. They're usually killed together as part of a Hunt Train, a group that works through every A-rank in an expansion. For Stormblood and older expansions, Hunt Trains are rare and marks are typically free-for-all.

S-rank marks have a specific window and only spawn once their condition is met. They're tracked on Faloop and spawn at most every few days.
hunts.guideWindowStatusTitle: What do the window statuses mean?
hunts.guideWindowStatusBody:
Closed means the mark is certainly outside its window.
Open means there's a chance the mark is active.
Capped means it has reached the end of its window and is certainly active, unless it was sniped.
Unmet means the window is active, but the mark's spawn condition depends on other factors, like weather, time, or moon phase, that aren't currently in place.
hunts.guideSSMarksBody: Every time an S-rank mark dies on a post-Shadowbringers map, there's a chance for 4 minions to spawn. Killing those minions in time spawns a special SS-rank mark, which gives more drops.
hunts.guideAffiliationBody: No. Aetherphone is an independent, unofficial client, it is not made, run, sponsored, or endorsed by Faloop in any way. It simply displays hunt data pulled from Faloop's public service. Please send feedback about this app to Aetherphone, not to Faloop.
hunts.guideContributeTitle: How can I contribute to hunt tracking?
hunts.guideContributeBody:
This app is an independent client that displays hunt data from Faloop's own tracking project. To contribute reports, or to learn more about Faloop itself, join their Discord:

https://discord.gg/faloop
hunts.guideScheduledBody: Accounts with reporting permissions on Faloop may see some marks as Scheduled. This means a reporter has reported the spawn but hasn't made it public yet. Please respect their decision and wait until the mark is public before advertising it.
hunts.guideMaintenanceTitle: How do maintenances affect mark windows?
hunts.guideMaintenanceBody:
When maintenance happens and the servers restart, every mark's timer resets to zero, and its window then follows the post-maintenance timing instead of the normal one.

Note that a server crash doesn't always reset S-rank timers, the backend may have stayed up even if players got disconnected.
hunts.guideUnlockBody:
Hunts unlock through a series of quests, one set per expansion, usually starting partway through that expansion's main scenario. For the full breakdown of every unlock quest, see the wiki:

https://ffxiv.consolegameswiki.com/wiki/The_Hunt#Unlock
hunts.guideSpawnConditionsTitle: How do people figure out the spawn conditions?
hunts.guideSpawnConditionsBody:
Each area has a specific NPC who shares lore about its S-ranks, and that lore usually hints at how to spawn them.

For example, Agrippa's lore mentions a hunter being ambushed after searching for treasure, hinting that its spawn condition is opening a treasure map.
hunts.guideGlossaryBody:
Conductor: Person who leads a Hunt Train.
ET/EzT: Eorzean Time. Pulls are usually scheduled in Eorzean time rather than real-world time.
Landmine: One of the spots where a mark can spawn.
PT: Pull Time, the moment the mark will be attacked and killed.
Scouter: Person who locates an A-rank mark ahead of a Hunt Train.
Sniping: Killing a hunt mark without reporting it. Sniping is completely permitted, but is generally considered poor etiquette.
Spawner/Reporter: Person who first reports a mark's spawn.
Train: An organized event where players kill every A-rank mark in an expansion, typically Shadowbringers or later.
tyfs: Thank You For Spawn, a common way to thank whoever reported the mark.
